evals.prompt: Users should get a Teams notification when their approval is pending. How do we set this up?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends sending an Adaptive Card in Teams via Power Automate, and considers Teams connector vs Graph API for delivery.
expectations: Agent recommends a Power Automate flow triggered by the approval event
Agent recommends using an Adaptive Card in Teams for rich, actionable notifications (not plain text)
Agent considers the Teams connector (Post Adaptive Card) as the simpler option
Agent considers Microsoft Graph API as an alternative for more control (e.g., chat messages, channel posts)
Agent may include actionable buttons in the Adaptive Card (Approve/Reject) so users can act directly from Teams
Agent warns against using personal email for automated notifications (use shared mailbox or Teams channel)

evals.prompt: The app needs to read the user's manager from Azure AD and show their recent SharePoint documents. How should we implement this?
evals.expected_output: Agent recommends Microsoft Graph API for both manager lookup and SharePoint document retrieval, discusses permission models and caching.
expectations: Agent recommends Microsoft Graph API for reading the user's manager (GET /users/{id}/manager)
Agent recommends Microsoft Graph API for retrieving recent SharePoint documents (GET /users/{id}/drive/recent or search endpoint)
Agent discusses delegated permissions vs application permissions — delegated is appropriate here since it's per-user data
Agent recommends delegated permissions with User.Read.All (or People.Read) for manager and Files.Read.All for documents
Agent suggests a caching strategy to avoid repeated Graph calls on every page load (manager info changes infrequently)
Agent may recommend a custom connector wrapping Graph API for reusability across the app
Agent handles Graph API pagination (documents endpoint may return paged results)
